n: This revelation explains 1 Corinthians 7:14, which Joseph was studying in his Bible translation. Paul says a believing spouse sanctifies an unbelieving one, so their children are holy.

f.w: the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife

n: In the apostles’ time, Jews who rejected Jesus still practiced circumcision under the law of Moses.

f.g: The covenant rite given to Abraham’s male descendants.

n: Conflict arose when an unbelieving Jewish husband wanted his children circumcised and raised under the law of Moses, which Christ had fulfilled.
Children raised under the law then followed their fathers’ traditions, rejected Christ, and became “unholy.”
So Paul advised, on his own counsel rather than by direct command from the Lord, that believers not marry unbelievers unless the law of Moses was set aside in the home.

f.w: not of the Lord, but of himself

n: This would allow children to remain uncircumcised and end the tradition that young children are unholy.
The key truth: little children are holy, sanctified by Christ’s Atonement. They need no ritual to be made clean.
